## The AI/ML Talent Market

AI and ML hiring is one of the most competitive segments in technology, and employers often disagree about what each job title means. This guide helps you define the role before you search. It contains no salary or market-share figures, because we have not cited a source for any. Use a current, named compensation source for your market and level.

### AI/ML Role Taxonomy

| Role | Focus | Typical background |
|---|---|---|
| ML engineer | Production ML systems | Computer science plus ML experience |
| Research scientist | Novel algorithms, publications | Advanced degree in ML or statistics |
| Applied scientist | Taking research into production | Advanced degree or strong applied experience |
| MLOps engineer | ML infrastructure and pipelines | DevOps plus ML experience |
| Data scientist (ML) | Analysis and modelling | Statistics or maths background |
| AI product manager | AI product strategy | Technical product background |
| Prompt or LLM engineer | LLM application behaviour and evaluation | Varied |

### Where AI/ML Talent Works

Candidates choose between large technology companies, AI startups, enterprises, research labs, consultancies and government. Each draws people for different reasons.

| Employer type | What draws candidates |
|---|---|
| Large technology companies | Resources, data, scale of impact |
| AI startups | Innovation, speed, ownership, equity |
| Enterprise | Stability, real domain problems |
| Research labs | Publication freedom, prestige |
| Consulting and services | Variety of problems |
| Government and defense | Mission, security clearance |

### Assessment for AI/ML Roles

#### Technical Interview Structure

**Round 1: ML fundamentals**

- Bias-variance tradeoff, regularization, model selection
- Feature engineering and data preprocessing
- Evaluation metrics such as precision, recall, F1 and AUC
- Statistical foundations such as hypothesis testing and distributions

**Round 2: System design**

- "Design a recommendation system for an e-commerce platform"
- "Design a real-time fraud detection pipeline"
- Evaluate scalability, monitoring, A/B testing and feedback loops

**Round 3: Coding and ML**

- Implement a model from scratch
- Debug a model with poor performance
- Data cleaning and feature engineering exercise

**Round 4: Research or paper discussion**

- Discuss a recent paper the candidate found interesting
- Evaluate depth of understanding, ability to critique and practical application ideas

### Competing with Larger Employers

You may not match the largest employers on total compensation. Compete on other factors:

| Factor | Larger employer | Your possible advantage |
|---|---|---|
| Compensation | Large total packages | Equity upside, if you are a startup |
| Impact | A small piece of a large system | End-to-end ownership |
| Speed | Longer launch cycles | Shipping often |
| Data | Large proprietary datasets | Unique domain data |
| Bureaucracy | Multiple approvals | Direct impact |
| Publishing | Sometimes restricted | Can be encouraged |
| Title | Standardised levels | Flexible titles |

Only claim an advantage that is true for your team.

### Retention

AI/ML engineers commonly leave over a few themes: uninteresting problems, too little compute, compensation elsewhere, no chance to publish, and organizational friction. Ask your own engineers which apply. Retain by providing challenging problems, investing in infrastructure, reviewing compensation against your market and supporting conference attendance and publications.
